nba_directive.reason_text: This client is close to ready but has a stated blocker (credit, income, or debt) — the highest-converting conditional-future profile. With a 2.88% first mortgage, a cash-out refi would destroy their rate, so the winning move is a concrete blocker-removal plan paired with a HELOC/second-lien framing that protects their $1,200/mo payment and attacks their higher-rate debt instead.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Open by protecting their 2.88% rate as a hard asset worth keeping
  - Name it explicitly: 'Your 2.88% conventional rate is one of the best in the market — we are not touching that'
  - Reframe the conversation away from refinance and toward a second-lien/HELOC that leaves the first mortgage and $1,200/mo payment completely intact

- Address the blocker head-on with a concrete removal plan, not a soft brush-off
  - Ask them to state the specific blocker (credit score, income gap, or debt-to-income) so you can build a named, dated action plan
  - If credit: identify the exact items dragging the score, give 2-3 targeted actions (balance paydown thresholds, dispute items if applicable), and schedule a hard re-pull date — put it on the calendar in this text thread
  - If debt/DTI: show how consolidating their high-rate balances into a HELOC can actually improve DTI, making them more approvable — not less
  - If income: clarify what documentation gap exists and what timeline closes it

- Anchor the HELOC value to their actual high-rate debt pain
  - Ask: 'What are your current credit card balances and rates?' — do not invent a number
  - Once they share balances, compute and present: monthly interest saved (card rate minus HELOC rate × balance) and total interest saved over a realistic payoff window
  - Reframe the HELOC rate against the 25-30% credit card benchmark, not against their 2.88% mortgage
  - Their $252,179 remaining balance signals meaningful equity — use that as the access point without overstating an available draw amount until an appraisal/AVM is run

- Secure a specific next step before closing the text
  - Offer two options: a 10-minute call to map the blocker-removal plan together, or an e-consent to pull a soft credit review now so you have real numbers
  - Set a named follow-up date tied to the blocker timeline — not a vague 'circle back'
  - Make clear you are building a plan with them, not waiting on them
